batch_goal: Deliver the last two unshipped pieces of board-review step 2 (make the board usable without changing the contract) as small, self-contained, unit-testable web-only modules: always-visible zoom in / zoom out / fit-to-wall buttons wired to the one existing camera transform (re-planning the previously scope-blocked zoom-controls task with a different approach — a standalone module plus an explicit, over-declared touch list instead of edits buried in the wall mount), and a dismissible first-visit onboarding hint that teaches tap-cell → pick color → Place plus pinch/drag-to-pan without ever blocking painting. No contract, no wallet, no palette or shared metadata changes, no new camera math.
escalations: NEAR drawing-session experiment (board review step 4) remains ask-first and unstarted: a restricted function-call key limited to the board's draw method with a bounded gas allowance, plain-language activation/allowance/renewal/revoke copy, and on-chain revoke verification need a human decision on allowance scope plus a funded testnet account with a game account id.

Next-milepost live check ('two people on separate devices observe each other's work automatically', ~3-5s visibility) still requires a live testnet board with a configured game account id and a deployed URL — a human step. Until it exists, web-only polish can be verified locally only.

Saturated palette proposal (docs/2026-10-12-palette-proposal.md) remains ask-first: changing the eight-colour palette changes metadata across web/shared/chain and the meaning of stored colours, and needs a tier-2 update in docs/00-shared-decisions.md before any implementation brief is written.

Process escalation (fifth batch, still unresolved on the other side): the scope_violation that blocked wall-zoom-controls-in-mount was triggered by the ask-first vocabularies of reversible web files (style.css, a mount dispose test) rather than by a genuine off-scope edit. This batch again mitigates by over-declaring web/src and every candidate file, which is not a sustainable substitute for a rule that scope_violation fires only on undeclared non-web-adjacent edits. Both tasks above touch overlapping files (mount-wall.ts, style.css), so if they run in parallel the shared edits are limited to one import + one mount call + one CSS block each.
Continuous drawing / brush strokes (board review step 5) stays out of scope: it needs an explicit paint mode, a serialized queue and a bounded batch contract method — contract work that is ask-first.
